answer: When AI agents trade services, a payment-graph analyzer clusters identities by shared signals: two agents funded from the same wallet become kin, like timber traced to one lagoon source. If fifty profiles route through identical shale-layer infrastructure or ping the network in lockstep bursts, the system collapses them into a single entity and caps their collective voting weight or reward share. An attacker spawning a thousand sockpuppets still gets one vote if the payment roots converge, making sybil farms economically worthless.
